messages:
Alyssa: Quick question — we're documenting recommended SDK/agent config for KMS credentials across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Want to capture a canonical precedence + recommendations for local dev, CI, and Private (VPC/on‑prem). Also: envelope encryption patterns and rotation cadence.

Matt: +1. We should call out audit log implications (key usage logs vs service principal logs).

Sriram: Trash list first: DO NOT hardcode long‑lived keys in app configs. Prefer short‑lived tokens or Vault-style secrets.

Alyssa: Agreed. Drafting a simple precedence order I want feedback on: 1) Explicit env vars (dev only) 2) SDK credential provider chain / workload identity (prod) 3) Vault/SSM secrets fetched at startup or via sidecar 4) Console-managed service principal configured on private control plane. Does that capture reality?

Jenna: Pretty close. Add: for container platforms prefer workload identity (AWS IRSA / GCP WI / Azure MSI) before static creds. Also mention local dev override with `~/.aws/credentials` if present.

Sriram: Two clarifications: (a) For Private on-prem, Vault with AppRole or mTLS auth is best. (b) Make explicit that Vault/SSM should ideally hand out short‑lived DEK/credentials, not long‑lived CMK keys.

Alyssa: Good point. Also thinking of envelope flow we want in docs: app requests data key from KMS (or Vault), uses DEK locally to encrypt, stores ciphertext + keyMetadata, and never stores raw DEK. Re-encrypt on rotation.

Matt: Example snippets would help. For AWS local dev quick override:
```bash
# local dev only
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA...
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=...
```
Use OS env for quick sandboxing, but add a big WARNING.

Jenna: Vault agent example for Private:
```hcl
vault {
  address = "https://vault.corp"
  auth "approle" {
    role_id_file_path = "/etc/creds/role_id"
    secret_id_file_path = "/etc/creds/secret_id"
  }
}
# application reads /tmp/vault/dek.json
```
Short‑lived DEKs, rotated by Vault TTL.

Sriram: For CI: use ephemeral IAM roles or OIDC tokens from GH Actions -> assume role. Avoid baking secrets in pipeline logs. Example: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn ... --web-identity-token file` then set temp envs.

Alyssa: Audit logging: we should recommend enabling KMS key usage logs (CloudTrail/GCP Audit) + application-level audit (who requested DEK, request id, reason) and link them. Also call out that envelope metadata should include key version and CMK ARN so post-rotation rewraps can be automated.

Matt: Also surface RBAC: make sure key policies restrict who can generate/describe/reencrypt. Some teams accidentally allow decrypt for broader groups. Recommend distinct roles: encrypt-only vs decrypt-only for services.

Jenna: Rotation cadence suggestion in docs: CMKs rotate annually or per compliance; DEKs rotate more frequently (daily or per-file). If you rely on automatic CMK rotation, ensure rewrap tool is in place to re-encrypt stored ciphertexts with the new CMK when needed.

Sriram: TL;DR recommendation block we can copy: 1) Use workload identity / instance role for prod; 2) Use Vault/AppRole or Cloud KMS ephemeral keys for Private; 3) Use env vars and shared creds only for local dev; 4) CI -> OIDC/assume-role; 5) Always use envelope encryption and never persist plaintext DEKs; 6) Enable audit logs for KMS and application; 7) Enforce key policy RBAC (separate encrypt/decrypt roles); 8) Have a rewrap plan for CMK rotation.

Alyssa: Perfect. One more: SDK precedence note for docs: AWS SDK resolves credentials in this order (summarized): env vars -> shared credentials file -> container/EKS web identity -> EC2/IAM instance profile. Make that explicit with links.

VaultBot: Reminder: rotate Vault AppRole secret_id every 24h and mark old tokens revoked.

deploy-bot: FYI: I just deployed a docs PR to `internal-security` with a draft of this guidance (link: https://git.internal/docs/kms-cred-flow). Please review. :shipit:

Alyssa: I'll pull the PR and add a short cheat sheet and samples for AWS/GCP/Azure. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
